## QA Review — Backyard Designer 3D

**(1) Overlapping / clipped UI**
- No hard overlaps: the Terrain Sculpting modal clears the left tool rail (tight but clean) and the bottom toolbar. Toasts, compass, zoom stack, and status bar all have separation. ✅
- ⚠️ LOW — Left sidebar: the "Patios & Paths" header sits flush against the bottom edge with no visible items; it reads as clipped rather than scrolled unless scrollbar affordance is clearer.

**(2) 5-second comprehension for a new user**
- Mostly yes: left palette = "add things," modal explains the active sculpt action, status bar echoes current tool. The coaching tip ("Pick a mode, then click + drag…") helps.
- ⚠️ MED — Three separate control clusters (category sidebar, SCULPT/BUILD/VIEW rail, bottom toolbar) *plus* a modal plus toasts is visually busy; a newcomer may not know which control set is authoritative.

**(3) Confusing / ambiguous / broken-looking**
- ⚠️ MED — Status bar reads **"FPS: 1"** — the scene looks fine, so this either displays misleading telemetry or indicates a real render stall; either way it makes the app look broken.
- ⚠️ LOW — Duplicate controls: "Terrain" and "Analyze" appear in *both* the left rail and the bottom toolbar, with mismatched active-state colors (green in the rail, brown/orange in the toolbar) — reads as a styling inconsistency for the same state.
- ⚠️ LOW — "Innovate" (lightbulb) is an ambiguous verb for a backyard app; unclear what it does.
- ⚠️ LOW — Tiny unlabeled icon at the right of the "Terrain Controls" header has no obvious affordance.
- ✅ Data coherence is good: status bar (Tool: Raise, Brush: 8 ft, Height 0.1 ft) matches the modal, and the "Grid at Y=4 ft" toast matches Ground Level: 4 ft.

**Bottom line:** No blocking overlap or clipping bugs; ship-blockers are none, but fix the FPS: 1 readout, the duplicated Terrain/Analyze controls (and their clashing active colors), and the clipped-looking sidebar footer before calling it polished.
